title: Gaming community question
author: girlinthepic
selftext: I noticed online there's a rather large group of people that are against AI helping you build a game or paying for games that are made with AI. I'm using AI to implement everything I've purchased on Fab into unreal engine because I am unfamiliar. Do people like myself still get the same bad rap as people who completely generate their games with ai.. for example. there's nothing in my game that AI generated. I paid for everything that's in my game, i didn't know how to place things or make systems talk to each other that's where ai came in. I'm asking am I screwed when I go to post this on steam. Has anyone made a return on their investment? Im like 1k in. Trying to see if anyone in the last couple of months had any, even small, success.. breaking even would be more than enough for me 🙏🏼

comments.author: DamnrightWorldsDev
comments.body:
You're fine as you don't have to disclose ai usage on steam when all your assets are from the marketplace and not generated with ai.

That said: they are a very loud minority. 99,9% of consumer market just doesn't care AS LONG as the game is GOOD and polished and fun to play.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Steam does not require disclosure for AI coding. 

  
If do you disclose the AI coding, yes, you will be dragged into a culture war if your game is noticed at all. As an example, look at what happened to Slam Tank. Great game - noticed by influencers, who then only wanted to talk about the AI usage, and now that is the only thing anyone talks about in terms of the game. 

The public is brain dead and basically purely reflects the opinions of the media they consume, and right now the public consumes social media feeds, and those feeds are telling them that AI is slop garbage that will kill them and their children because the influencer networks are afraid that AI will disrupt their business.
